name: Eric Mulder

summary.text: Wayne Harlos, Mulder's running mate, also ran for Lieutenant Governor of Colorado on the Libertarian ticket in the 2020 election, according to Ballotpedia.
Eric Mulder is a U.S. Army veteran, security guard and small business owner from Aurora who previously served on Aurora's Veterans Affairs Commission and Civic Engagement Commission.

experience.text: Member, Aurora Civic Engagement Commission; previously served on the Aurora Veterans Affairs Commission.
Bachelor's degree, Rocky Mountain College of Art + Design, 2020.
Small business owner and private security contractor.

positions.source_title: Colorado Governor candidate Q&A - The Denver Post
positions.quote: I propose returning Medicaid to its pre-COVID baseline, reviewing everything added since then and eliminating what is unnecessary.
positions.note: Answering a question about the state's Medicaid funding crisis; he also proposes strengthening disability-eligibility standards and using state purchasing power to negotiate lower drug prices, which is why this is coded as a qualified rather than unqualified disagreement.

positions.source_title: Colorado Governor candidate Q&A - The Denver Post
positions.quote: I support limiting state cooperation with federal agencies in order to uphold constitutional safeguards on privacy and due process.
positions.note: He also says ICE's 'wrongful arrest, detention, and deportation of citizens is inexcusable,' with no stated carve-out for cooperation on serious crimes, so coded as an unqualified disagreement with Amendment 81's approach.

positions.source_title: Vote411 personalized ballot, League of Women Voters Education Fund (candidate answers shown after entering a Colorado address)
positions.quote: Housing diversity should be pursued, encouraging home rule districts to allow for multiple family units, accessory dwelling units, mobile home and tiny communities, etc.
positions.note: Favors the state encouraging local governments to allow denser housing; he says encourage rather than override, so this is inferred and capped at agree. Vote411 shows answers only after an address is entered, so the quote cannot be checked by script; it was read in a browser on 2026-10-15 using a public address in the race.

research_notes: Mulder's 2026 campaign site is mostly a placeholder/signup page with no issues content reachable by automated fetch; his Libertarian Party press release (lpcolorado.org) was blocked by a bot-detection challenge page. His Ballotpedia 2026 Candidate Connection survey gave three key messages (keeping state sales tax revenue local during emergencies, limiting government surveillance/privacy, and energy diversity) but only the energy answer maps clearly to one of the 25 statements. A separate 2024 Ballotpedia survey response exists from a different race (an Aurora-area state legislative campaign, not governor) and was not used here to avoid conflating offices. No endorsements beyond crowd-sourced 'Sway' voting-group listings were found. Second pass 2026-10-14: added health-coverage, immigration-notify-ice from https://www.denverpost.com/2026/10/03/colorado-governor-candidate-qa/, which he did answer. Gap fill 2026-10-15: Added an inferred housing position from his Vote411 answer.
